A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NoiseSDF2NoiseSDF by the same authors. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on ShapeNet, ABC, Famous, and Real, together with fine-tuning and noise-distribution ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original reconstruction results and adds supervision, architecture, initialization, and test-time-optimization experiments.

M1.justification: The paired noisy-SDF MSE objective and standard frozen-encoder/decoder-fine-tuning framework remain unchanged. Section 5.5 adds an optional Ours-TTO procedure that optimizes at test time using 200 noisy samples per shape, extending the original inference procedure.

E1.justification: The four datasets and existing noise-distribution tests are retained. However, the added Famous comparison references an N2NM setup and labels conditions MedN/MaxN without defining them locally. The PDFs do not establish whether these introduce distinct corruption scenarios or reuse existing conditions.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 remove 3DILG from the main ShapeNet comparisons. Table 3 replaces the quantitative 3DS2V comparison with POCO and NKSR, although 3DS2V remains in qualitative figures. New Table 5 adds N2NM. SAP-O and PGR remain, while 3DILG participates in the expanded ablations.

E3.justification: v2 adds the 200-sample TTO comparison, matched clean/noisy-supervision controls, alternative network configurations, and random-initialization experiments lasting 350 or 800 epochs. Existing fine-tuning budgets also change: FC plus cross-attention goes from 30 to 15 epochs, and the entire decoder from 15 to 30 (v1 Table 5; v2 Table 7). These reported revisions do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New experiments test clean versus noisy supervision, interchangeability of 3DS2V and 3DILG as targets and denoisers, random versus pretrained initialization, and improvement through TTO. The original component fine-tuning study is expanded. The existing noise-distribution and Gaussian-bias study remains as Table 8.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Reported Gaussian standard deviations describe input corruption, not uncertainty in experimental results.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial comparator, supervision, initialization, and TTO results while retaining the main benchmark scores for Ours. New Table 5 reports Ours-TTO Chamfer distances of 0.0108/0.0252 versus N2NM's 0.0132/0.0231 under MedN/MaxN, with 20 versus 2760 seconds. New Table 3 places POCO's overall mean NC at 0.828 above Ours at 0.819. PPSurf's low-noise mean Chamfer changes from 0.016 to 0.014 despite unchanged component rows.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5, their mathematical assumptions, and the appendix metric formulas are retained. The added discussion of continuous query domains supplies conceptual motivation, without a new formal result, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central claim that noisy supervision can produce cleaner neural fields. Section 2 adds an explicit priority claim that this is the first application of Noise2Noise to 3D neural fields; v1 presented the framework as a novel adaptation without that explicit claim.

C2.justification: v2 removes Appendix G.1's oversmoothing and encoder-capacity limitations, the detailed explanation of heavy-noise degradation, and discussion of limited Laplace and biased-Gaussian benefits. It instead describes heavy-noise performance more positively despite retained scores. New interpretations concern near-clean-supervision performance, architecture generality, and initialization accelerating convergence.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents single-pass inference and states that supplementary code includes training, evaluation, testing, preprocessing, and README instructions, with a public repository planned (Section 8; Appendix I.5). These are disclosures, not verified external availability. Core hardware and hyperparameters remain, while the decoder block count and precise PGR resolution caveat are removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning ImageNet initialization, NKSR, and fast noise-to-noise mapping. It sharpens the priority claim and contrasts generalizable inference with per-shape optimization. Most cited work and the overall research context remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, implementation discussion, and experimental narrative undergo extensive rewriting. Overfitting comparisons receive a separate subsection, ablations are reorganized, and ethics and reproducibility sections are added. The appendices are restructured with new LLM-use and supplementary-material statements.

P2.justification: Comparison and ablation tables are substantially redesigned with difference columns, top-two highlighting, expanded configurations, and new comparison panels. Figure 2 is reduced. Figure 4's high-noise rows move to Figure Appendix I.1, replacing v1's four additional appendix reconstruction examples.

improvement.justification: The clean-supervision, alternative-network, and initialization controls substantially strengthen empirical support, and the N2NM/TTO comparison adds useful accuracy and runtime evidence. However, v2 removes substantive failure explanations and limitations while presenting unchanged heavy-noise results more positively. The unexplained epoch revisions and changed PPSurf mean also weaken reporting clarity. These gains in evidence and losses in qualification leave the net quality direction uncertain.
